## Description {#details}

Functions for verifying exceptions in test cases.

The µTest++ framework provides dedicated functions for verifying whether specific expressions or function calls throw exceptions, supporting robust testing of error handling and exceptional conditions in C++ code.

These utilities enable developers to assert that exceptions are correctly thrown or not thrown as expected, improving the reliability and safety of software components. The framework supports both generic exception checks and type-specific exception verification, allowing for precise and expressive test cases.

For more advanced scenarios, such as handling multiple expected exceptions, developers can use explicit <code>try</code> blocks with multiple <code>catch</code> statements and report the results using <code>expect(true)</code> or <code>expect(false)</code>. This approach ensures comprehensive coverage of exception handling logic.

### nothrow() {#ga798bd28001c3938784073e60dd904148}

<MemberDefinition

Check if a callable does not throw an exception.

<ParametersList title="Template Parameters">
<ParametersListItem name="Callable_T">The type of the callable object to be invoked.</ParametersListItem>

<SectionUser title="Returns">

</SectionUser>

The <code>nothrow</code> function template verifies whether invoking the provided callable object does not result in the throwing of any exception within the µTest++ framework. This is useful for testing exception safety and ensuring that code under test does not unexpectedly signal error conditions.

The function returns an output stream, allowing optional messages to be appended to the test report for diagnostic purposes.
